assessment: SQLite assertTransactionActive observes sqlite.inTransaction before transactional SQL, revokes active and sets poison if native transaction has ended. This covers a native full rollback even outside the nested no-effect atomic seam; the outbox SQL invocation eventually passes through this local guard before execution.

Both nested adapter paths catch failures in rollback-to/release recovery, set shared active=false/poisoned=true and propagate the cleanup fault. Ordinary proved savepoint rollback does not poison the attempt and permits surrounding unrelated work to commit.

Shared state propagates through factory views. Local sync SQL checks liveness before execution, except compiler-controlled rollback/release cleanup; local async SQL checks before timeout refresh and again immediately before calling the statement executor after awaits. No new transactional statement is admitted after poison.

Both outer attempt callbacks check poison before accepting work success. With surviving SQLite transaction, outer rollback yields no_commit/rollbackProven=true. With SQLite already fully rolled back, the attempted outer cleanup fails and conservatively remains unknown/rollbackProven=false; no writes escape. On the PostgreSQL path, a poisoned callback rejects so begin's outer rollback occurs before the no_commit statement classification, rather than accepting callback success and COMMIT.

The original no-effect templates, immutable count/lifetime/fencing logic, possible marker conservatism, retry delay gates and prior nine test region remain byte-identical. No budget reset, unknown reopening or expanded provider authority was introduced by this correction.

Two registered tests use the actual generated client: SQLite RAISE(ROLLBACK) at dead-letter insertion followed by caught attempts at enqueue/create/policy-entry/view; PostgreSQL rollback-to proxy failure after a real authority write followed by caught attempts at SQL/outbox/policy-entry and expected outer rollback. The adapter-specific early returns are explicit, not evidence of execution on the other adapter.

cases: Original real SQLite whole-transaction RAISE(ROLLBACK) no-effect fault: outbox, sync SQL, preexisting/new operation-time views and new nested entry all refuse; outer unknown preserved; no new intent or authority row; original running/possible1/no-history unchanged.
Direct native transaction loss outside nested atomic seam: local guard rejects first new write and poisons callback, no autocommit.
Real SQLite ordinary RAISE(ABORT) no-effect fault: successful savepoint recovery preserves live outer capability and unrelated commit, with no partial history/marker reset.
SQLite injected RELEASE cleanup failure with surviving native transaction: all new work refuses and outer rollback proves no_commit.
Modeled PostgreSQL ROLLBACK TO failure: sync/async SQL, all views, outbox and nested entry refuse; callback poison causes outer rollback and leaves no authority row.
Modeled PostgreSQL RELEASE failure: same refusal/outer rollback assertions.
Async SQL guard after awaited timeout refresh: revocation during refresh prevents actual operation SQL; only the refresh reached the modeled driver.
